items.title: 4.1.1 Construction of First-Order and Differential Equations from Practical Situations (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 125-127: 4.1.1 introduction, Examples 1-4 (population, Newton's cooling law, inflation/deflation, RC and RL circuits) with Observations and Figures 4.1-4.2

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: 4.1.1 ki chhapi hui heading "Construction of First-Order and Differential Equations from Practical Situations" hai. "and" ke baad ek lafz ghayab hai; Section 4.2 ki tarah iska matlab hai "Construction of First-Order and First-Degree Differential Equations from Practical Situations", yani amli soorat-e-haal se first-order, first-degree differential equations banana. Neeche ki chaaron misaalein isi qisam ki equations deti hain.

Is sabaq mein hum differential equations hal nahi karenge, balke unhein banana seekhenge. Asal zindagi ki koi soorat-e-haal (situation) lein, us ko alfaz mein samjhein, aur phir alfaz ko mathematics ki zabaan mein tarjuma kar dein. Is tarjume ko "mathematical model" kehte hain. Engineer, doctor, economist sab yahi kaam karte hain: pehle model, phir hal.

Kitab kehti hai: first-order differential equations un masail (problems) ka model banati hain jin mein kisi cheez ke badalne ka rate khud us cheez par ya time par depend karta ho. Misaal ke taur par particle ki harkat (motion), population ka barhna ya ghatna, Newton's law of cooling ya heating, bijli ke circuits, economic models aur radioactive decay.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Model banana ek tarjume ka kaam hai. Is section ki har misaal aur har exercise mein yeh chaar qadam istemal kijiye:
1. Badalne wali cheez aur time ka naam rakhiye: \(P(t)\), \(T(t)\), \(q(t)\), ...
2. "\(Q\) ka rate of change" ko \(\frac{dQ}{dt}\) likhiye.
3. "X ke proportional" ko "\(= k \times X\)" likhiye, jahan \(k\) constant hai.
4. Sign ka faisla kijiye: cheez ghat rahi ho to us ka rate negative hai; ya to \(-k\) likhiye (jahan \(k > 0\)), ya \(k\) rehne dijiye aur kahiye \(k < 0\).
Yaad rakhiye: yahan hum equations hal nahi karte; hal karna Sections 4.2 aur 4.3 ka kaam hai.

Ab pehli misaal. Sab se pehle hum dekhte hain ke sawal mein kahani kya hai: kisi jagah ki aabadi (population) waqt ke saath badal rahi hai. Humein us ka rate of change aur khud aabadi ke darmiyan rishta mathematics mein likhna hai. Ghor kijiye ke yahan "find" karne wali cheez koi number nahi, balke ek equation hai; yani jawab ek formula ki shakal mein hoga, jaise \(\frac{dP}{dt} = \ldots\).

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.problem: Population Growth/Decay. The rate of change of a population is proportional to the population itself. Construct the differential equation (mathematical model) for the population \(P\) at time \(t\).
steps:
Diya gaya: population ke badalne ka rate (raftaar) khud population ke proportional (mutanasib) hai.
Maloom karna: \(P(t)\) ke liye differential equation.
Tareeqa: jumle ko symbols mein tarjuma karna hai. "Time ke saath \(P\) ka rate of change" ka matlab \(\frac{dP}{dt}\) hai, aur "\(P\) ke proportional" ka matlab hai "ek constant guna \(P\)". Bas yahi do cheezein jorni hain.

Mathematical Model: proportionality likhiye
Maan lijiye \(P\) time \(t\) par population hai. Kyunke population ke badalne ka rate us waqt ki population ke proportional hai, is liye
\[\dfrac{dP}{dt} \propto P\]
Kyun: jitni zyada aabadi, utne zyada maa baap, utni zyada paidaish har saal. Yani aabadi jitni bari, barhne ki raftaar bhi utni zyada. Jaise ek gaon mein 100 log hon to saal mein shayad 3 bachay paida hon, magar shehar mein 10 lakh log hon to hazaron.

Constant of proportionality daliye
Agar \(k\) constant of proportionality ho to
\[\dfrac{dP}{dt} = kP\]
Kyun: \(A \propto B\) ka hamesha matlab hai \(A = kB\), jahan \(k\) koi constant hai. \(\propto\) ka nishan calculation mein istemal nahi ho sakta, is liye use "\(= k\,\times\)" se badal dete hain.
Dhyan dein: final jawab mein \(\propto\) kabhi na chhoriye.

Equation ki pehchan
Yeh first-order differential equation hai.
Kyun: is mein sirf ek derivative \(\frac{dP}{dt}\) hai jo pehla derivative hai, is liye order 1. Us ki power bhi 1 hai, is liye degree bhi 1.

Tasdeeq:
Function \(P = P_{0}e^{kt}\) (jo aage is unit mein hal kar ke milega) se
\[\dfrac{dP}{dt} = kP_{0}e^{kt} = kP\]
Yani model theek chalta hai: \(k > 0\) par barhna, \(k < 0\) par ghatna.
blocks.answer: \(\dfrac{dP}{dt} = kP\), a first-order differential equation (\(k\) = constant of proportionality).

blocks.title: Observation
blocks.text:
Is equation se hum dekhte hain:
(i) Agar \(k > 0\) ho to population barhti hai (growth), kyunke \(\frac{dP}{dt}\) positive hai.
(ii) Agar \(k < 0\) ho to population ghatti hai (decay), kyunke \(\frac{dP}{dt}\) negative hai.
(iii) Agar \(k = 0\) ho to \(\frac{dP}{dt} = 0\), yani population constant rehti hai.
Is differential equation ko hal kar ke hum kisi bhi waqt \(t\) par population maloom kar sakte hain.

Ab zara \(k\) ke baare mein sochte hain, kyunke yeh chhota sa harf bahut kuch batata hai. \(k\) ko growth rate ya decay rate kehte hain. Agar \(k = 0.02\) har saal ho to iska matlab hai ke population har saal taqreeban 2% ke hisaab se barh rahi hai. \(k\) jitna bara, izafa utna tez. Isi liye har mulk ki population ka \(k\) alag hota hai. Ek aur baat: equation \(\frac{dP}{dt} = kP\) humein yeh nahi batati ke aaj population kitni hai; woh sirf yeh batati hai ke kisi bhi waqt population kis raftaar se badal rahi hai. Asal population maloom karne ke liye humein equation hal karni hogi aur ek shuruati value (jaise \(t = 0\) par \(P = P_{0}\)) chahiye hogi. Yeh kaam hum Section 4.2 aur 4.3 mein karenge.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar kisi shehar ki population har saal ghat rahi ho (log shehar chhor kar ja rahe hon), to \(\frac{dP}{dt} = kP\) mein \(k\) ka sign kya hoga? Jawab: \(k < 0\), kyunke \(P\) positive hai aur \(\frac{dP}{dt}\) negative hona chahiye. Isi ko decay kehte hain.

Doosri misaal roz marra ki hai. Garam chaye ka cup mez par rakh dein to woh aahista aahista kamre ke temperature tak aa jata hai; aur fridge se nikli thandi bottle kamre mein rakh dein to woh garam ho kar kamre ke temperature tak pohanchti hai. Newton ne dekha ke yeh tabdeeli shuru mein tez aur baad mein aahista hoti hai, kyunke farq kam hota jata hai. Isi mushahide (observation) ko ab equation mein badalte hain.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.problem: Temperature Problem (Cooling/Heating Law). Let \(T\) represent the temperature of a body at time \(t\), and let \(T_{S}\) be the constant temperature of the surrounding medium. According to Newton's law of cooling (or heating), the rate of change of the body's temperature with respect to time is proportional to the difference between the body's temperature and the surrounding temperature. Construct the differential equation.
steps:
Diya gaya: jism (body) ka temperature \(T(t)\), mahaul (surrounding) ka constant temperature \(T_{S}\); \(T\) ke badalne ka rate dono temperatures ke farq ke proportional hai.
Maloom karna: \(T(t)\) ke liye differential equation.
Tareeqa: "\(T\) ka rate of change" \(\frac{dT}{dt}\) hai; pehle proportionality likhenge, phir ek positive constant \(k\) dalenge.

Mathematical Model: proportionality likhiye
\[\dfrac{dT}{dt} \propto (T_{S} - T)\]
Kyun: jism aur mahaul ke temperature mein jitna zyada farq, garmi utni tezi se behti hai, is liye \(T\) utni tezi se badalta hai. Ubalti chaye kamre mein jaldi thandi hoti hai, magar neem garam chaye aahista. Kitab farq ko \(T_{S} - T\) is liye likhti hai taa ke sign khud ba khud sahi aaye (agla qadam dekhiye).

Constant daliye
Positive constant of proportionality \(k > 0\) dalne se
\[\dfrac{dT}{dt} = k(T_{S} - T)\]
Yeh hamari required first-order differential equation hai.
Kyun: \(k > 0\) ho to \(\frac{dT}{dt}\) ka sign wohi hai jo \(T_{S} - T\) ka hai. Jism kamre se thanda ho to garam hota hai, aur garam ho to thanda hota hai. Ek hi formula dono kaam karta hai, isi liye ise cooling/heating law kehte hain.

Tasdeeq:
Garam chaye: \(T = 80\), \(T_{S} = 30\) rakhein to
\[\dfrac{dT}{dt} = k(30 - 80) = -50k < 0\]
Yani chaye thandi ho rahi hai, bilkul asal zindagi ki tarah.
blocks.answer: \(\dfrac{dT}{dt} = k(T_{S} - T)\), \(k > 0\): a first-order differential equation.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab Example 2 ke aakhir mein "This is the required first ordered differential." likhti hai, jis mein "equation" ka lafz ghayab hai. Sahi jumla hai: "This is the required first-order differential equation", yani yeh hamari required first-order differential equation hai, jaise humne upar likha.

blocks.title: Observations
blocks.text:
(i) Agar \(T < T_{S}\) ho, yani jism mahaul se thanda ho, to jism garam ho raha hai aur \(\frac{dT}{dt}\) positive hai.
(ii) Agar \(T > T_{S}\) ho, yani jism mahaul se garam ho, to jism thanda ho raha hai aur \(\frac{dT}{dt}\) negative hai.
Is differential equation ko hal kar ke hum kisi bhi waqt \(t\) par jism ka temperature \(T\) maloom kar sakte hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Numbers ke saath samajhte hain (yeh hamari misaal hai, kitab ki nahi). Kamre ka temperature \(T_{S} = 25\) hai aur \(k = 0.1\) (har minute). Chaye ka temperature \(T = 85\) ho to
\[\dfrac{dT}{dt} = 0.1(25 - 85) = -6\]
yani us waqt chaye har minute taqreeban 6 degree thandi ho rahi hai. Jab chaye \(T = 35\) tak aa jaye to
\[\dfrac{dT}{dt} = 0.1(25 - 35) = -1\]
yani ab sirf 1 degree har minute. Dekha? Farq kam hua to thanda hone ki raftaar bhi kam ho gayi. Yahi Newton's law ka asal paigham hai, aur isi wajah se chaye kabhi bilkul kamre ke temperature se neeche nahi jati.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Fridge se nikli bottle ka temperature \(T = 5\) aur kamre ka \(T_{S} = 30\) ho to \(\frac{dT}{dt}\) ka sign kya hoga? Jawab: \(k(30 - 5) = 25k > 0\), yani positive; bottle garam ho rahi hai. Ek hi equation thanda hona aur garam hona dono sambhal leti hai.

Teesri misaal economics se hai. Pehle do lafz samajh lijiye. Inflation (mehngai) ka matlab hai ke waqt ke saath cheezon ki qeematein barh rahi hain; deflation ka matlab hai ke qeematein gir rahi hain. Hum ek aisi first-order differential equation banayenge jo batati hai ke inflation ya deflation ki wajah se kisi cheez ki qeemat waqt ke saath kaise badalti hai.

blocks.title: Example 3
blocks.problem: Inflation/Deflation Problem in Economics. Inflation means the price of goods is increasing over time, while deflation means the price of goods is decreasing over time. Construct a first-order differential equation to describe how the price of a good changes over time due to inflation or deflation.
steps:
Diya gaya: qeemat (price) ke badalne ka rate maujooda qeemat ke proportional hai.
Maloom karna: qeemat \(P(t)\) ke liye differential equation.
Tareeqa: bilkul Example 1 wala tarjuma: rate = \(\frac{dP}{dt}\), "proportional" = constant guna.

Mathematical Model: farz (assumption)
Maan lijiye \(P\) time \(t\) par kisi cheez ki qeemat hai. Hum farz karte hain ke qeemat ke badalne ka rate maujooda qeemat ke proportional hai:
\[\dfrac{dP}{dt} \propto P\]
Kyun: maan lijiye 10% inflation (mehngai) hai. Rs. 1000 ki cheez saal mein Rs. 100 mehngi hogi, magar Rs. 100 ki cheez sirf Rs. 10. Yani izafa maujooda qeemat par depend karta hai.

Constant daliye
\(k\) ko constant of proportionality maan lein jo inflation ya deflation ka rate batata hai; to required equation
\[\dfrac{dP}{dt} = kP\]
Kyun: \(\propto\) ki jagah "\(= k\,\times\)". Yahan \(k > 0\) inflation (qeemat barhna) aur \(k < 0\) deflation (qeemat girna) batata hai.
Dhyan dein: yeh wohi equation hai jo population mein aayi thi; sirf \(P\) ka matlab badal gaya. Mathematics ek hi hai, kahaniyan alag alag.

Tasdeeq:
\(k > 0\) aur \(P > 0\) ho to \(\frac{dP}{dt} > 0\): qeematein barh rahi hain (inflation). \(k < 0\) ho to \(\frac{dP}{dt} < 0\): qeematein gir rahi hain (deflation). Model dono definitions par poora utarta hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar kisi mulk mein mehngai ka rate \(k = 0.12\) har saal ho aur aate ki ek bori ki qeemat is waqt Rs. 3000 ho, to is lamhe qeemat kis raftaar se barh rahi hai? Jawab: \(\frac{dP}{dt} = 0.12 \times 3000 = 360\), yani taqreeban Rs. 360 har saal. Aur agar deflation ho, \(k = -0.05\), to \(\frac{dP}{dt} = -150\): qeemat Rs. 150 saalana ki raftaar se gir rahi hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Example 1 aur Example 3 ki equations bilkul ek jaisi hain: \(\frac{dP}{dt} = kP\). Kya aap koi teesri misaal soch sakte hain jahan rate cheez ke proportional ho? (Misaal: bank mein rakha paisa, jo compound interest se barhta hai. Yahi Exercise 4.1 ka Question 2 hai.)

Chauthi misaal bijli ke circuits ki hai, aur yahan thori physics yaad karni zaroori hai, is liye pehle aasaan alfaz mein teen hisse samajh lijiye. Resistor (\(R\)) current ka rasta tang karta hai; us par voltage Ohm's law se \(V_{R} = IR\) hota hai. Capacitor (\(C\)) do plates ka ek dabba hai jo charge jama karta hai, jaise balti pani jama karti hai; us par voltage \(V_{C} = \frac{q}{C}\) hota hai, yani jitna zyada charge utna zyada voltage. Inductor (\(L\)) taar ka coil hai jo current ki tabdeeli ko pasand nahi karta; current tezi se badle to woh ulta voltage \(V_{L} = L\frac{dI}{dt}\) paida karta hai, bilkul bhari gaari ki tarah jo achanak chalti hai na achanak rukti hai. Aur source ki emf \(V_{S}\) woh "dhakka" hai jo battery charge ko deti hai. Kirchhoff's voltage law kehta hai ke loop mein tamam hisson ke voltages ka jama source ke voltage ke barabar hota hai. Bas inhi cheezon se hum dono equations banayenge.

blocks.title: Example 4
blocks.problem: Flow of Electricity in Series Circuits. In daily life, many problems involve the current flowing in series circuits. Construct the first-order differential equations for two simple cases: (i) charging a capacitor through a resistor (RC circuit model), and (ii) charging an inductor through a resistor (RL circuit model).
steps:
Diya gaya: (i) resistor \(R\) aur capacitor \(C\) series mein, DC source ke saath jis ki emf \(V_{S}\) hai; (ii) resistor \(R\) aur inductor \(L\) series mein, waisa hi source.
Maloom karna: (i) mein charge \(q(t)\) ke liye aur (ii) mein current \(I(t)\) ke liye differential equation.
Tareeqa: har hisse (component) par voltage likhenge, phir Kirchhoff's voltage law lagayenge: tamam components ke voltages ka jama source ke voltage ke barabar hota hai.

(i) Charging a Capacitor Through a Resistor (RC Circuit Model): soorat-e-haal
RC circuit mein \(R\) ohm ka resistor aur \(C\) farad ka capacitor series mein ek DC source ke saath jure hain jis ki constant emf \(V_{S}\) volt hai. Shuru mein current zero maana gaya hai (neeche Figure 4.1 dekhiye). Time \(t = 0\) par switch band kiya jata hai aur capacitor charge hona shuru hota hai. Maan lijiye time \(t\) par capacitor par charge \(q\) hai aur circuit mein current \(I\) hai.
Kyun: equation likhne se pehle badalne wali cheezon ke naam rakhne zaroori hain.

(i) Mathematical Model: har hisse par voltage
Capacitor par voltage
\[V_{C} = \dfrac{q}{C}\]
Ohm's law ke mutabiq resistor par voltage
\[V_{R} = IR\]
Kyun: yeh dono components ke physics ke qawaneen hain: capacitor ka voltage charge ko capacitance se divide karne se milta hai, aur resistor Ohm's law maanta hai.

(i) Kirchhoff's voltage law
Kirchhoff's voltage law ke mutabiq resistor aur capacitor ke voltages ka jama battery ke total voltage ke barabar hai:
\[V_{S} = V_{R} + V_{C}\]
\[V_{S} = \dfrac{q}{C} + V_{R}\]
\[V_{S} = \dfrac{q}{C} + IR\]
Kyun: band loop ka ek chakkar lagayein to source jo energy deta hai (har unit charge ko) woh components mein kharch ho jati hai. Jaise jeb mein 100 rupay hon aur do dukanon par kharch karein, to dono kharchon ka jama 100 hi hoga.

(i) Derivative laaiye
\(I = \frac{dq}{dt}\) rakhne se equation banti hai
\[R\dfrac{dq}{dt} + \dfrac{q}{C} = V_{S}\]
ya saada shakal mein (\(C\) se multiply kar ke terms adal badal kar)
\[RC\dfrac{dq}{dt} = CV_{S} - q\]
Kyun: current charge ke behne ka rate hai, is liye \(I = \frac{dq}{dt}\). Isi qadam ne aam equation ko \(q\) ki differential equation bana diya.
Dhyan dein: \(C\) se multiply karte waqt \(\frac{q}{C}\) sirf \(q\) banta hai aur \(V_{S}\) \(CV_{S}\) banta hai.

(ii) Charging an Inductor Through a Resistor (RL Circuit Model): soorat-e-haal
Situation: RL circuit mein \(R\) ohm ka resistor aur \(L\) henry ka inductor series mein ek DC source ke saath jure hain jis ki constant emf \(V_{S}\) volt hai. Shuru mein current zero maana gaya hai (neeche Figure 4.2 dekhiye). Time \(t = 0\) par switch band hota hai aur inductor charge hona shuru hota hai. Maan lijiye time \(t\) par inductor mein current \(I\) hai.
Kyun: is dafa hum jis cheez ka peecha kar rahe hain woh khud current \(I\) hai.

(ii) Mathematical Model: har hisse par voltage
Inductor par voltage
\[V_{L} = L\dfrac{dI}{dt}\]
Ohm's law ke mutabiq resistor par voltage
\[V_{R} = RI\]
Kyun: inductor current ki tabdeeli ki mukhalifat karta hai; us ka voltage is baat ke proportional hai ke current kitni tezi se badal raha hai. Current na badle to inductor par voltage zero.

(ii) Kirchhoff's voltage law
Resistor aur inductor ke voltages ka jama lagaye gaye voltage ke barabar hai:
\[V_{S} = V_{L} + V_{R}\]
\[L\dfrac{dI}{dt} + RI = V_{S}\]
Is tarah differential equation hai
\[L\dfrac{dI}{dt} = V_{S} - RI\]
Kyun: wohi loop wala qanoon jo (i) mein laga; yahan derivative pehle se \(V_{L}\) ke zariye maujood hai, alag se \(I = \frac{dq}{dt}\) ki zaroorat nahi.

Tasdeeq:
(i) \(q = CV_{S}\left(1 - e^{-t/RC}\right)\) se \(RC\frac{dq}{dt} = CV_{S}e^{-t/RC} = CV_{S} - q\).
(ii) \(I = \frac{V_{S}}{R}\left(1 - e^{-Rt/L}\right)\) se \(L\frac{dI}{dt} = V_{S}e^{-Rt/L} = V_{S} - RI\).
Dono models charging ke jaane pehchane formulas se poore hote hain (sympy se check kiya).
blocks.answer: (i) RC circuit: \(RC\dfrac{dq}{dt} = CV_{S} - q\). (ii) RL circuit: \(L\dfrac{dI}{dt} = V_{S} - RI\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Part (i) mein kitab \(V_{S} = V_{r} + V_{C}\) chhoti \(r\) ke saath likhti hai. Resistor ka voltage \(V_{R}\) hai (jaise agli hi line mein likha hai), is liye sahi \(V_{S} = V_{R} + V_{C}\) hai; humne upar sahi likha hai. Isi tarah kitab ki Figure 4.1 mein switch par "Swithc" likha hai; sahi lafz "Switch" hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Part (i) mein kitab kehti hai ke "shuru mein current zero maana gaya hai". Yeh switch band hone se pehle ki baat hai. \(t = 0\) par asal mein capacitor ka charge zero hota hai, \(q(0) = 0\). Jis lamhe switch band hota hai, current achanak \(\frac{V_{S}}{R}\) ho jata hai aur phir jaise jaise capacitor bharta hai, current kam hota jata hai, jaise khaali balti mein pani shuru mein tezi se girta hai aur bharne ke qareeb aahista. Part (ii) mein current waqai \(I(0) = 0\) se shuru hota hai, kyunke inductor current ko achanak badalne nahi deta.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Dono circuits ka muqabla (comparison) ek nazar mein:
RC circuit mein hum charge \(q\) ka peecha karte hain; derivative \(I = \frac{dq}{dt}\) ke zariye aata hai; final equation \(RC\frac{dq}{dt} = CV_{S} - q\).
RL circuit mein hum current \(I\) ka peecha karte hain; derivative inductor ke voltage \(L\frac{dI}{dt}\) ke zariye aata hai; final equation \(L\frac{dI}{dt} = V_{S} - RI\).
Dono mein right side "target value minus maujooda value" ki shakal mein hai: capacitor ka aakhri charge \(CV_{S}\) hai aur inductor ka aakhri current \(\frac{V_{S}}{R}\). Is liye dono shuru mein tezi se aur baad mein aahista badalte hain, bilkul Newton's cooling law ki tarah.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar battery hata di jaye, yani \(V_{S} = 0\), to dono equations kya banengi? RC ke liye \(RC\frac{dq}{dt} = -q\) aur RL ke liye \(L\frac{dI}{dt} = -RI\). Yeh discharging (khaali hone) ki equations hain, aur yahi Exercise 4.1 ke Questions 6 aur 7 hain. Pehle khud koshish kijiye, phir un ke solved pages dekhiye.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Ek chhoti practice (yeh hamari misaal hai, kitab ka sawal nahi): ek tank mein pani ki miqdaar \(V\) hai, aur pani is tarah nikal raha hai ke nikalne ka rate maujooda pani ke proportional hai. Model banaiye.
Qadam 1: badalne wali cheez \(V(t)\).
Qadam 2: rate \(\frac{dV}{dt}\).
Qadam 3: proportional, to \(\frac{dV}{dt} \propto V\), yani \(\frac{dV}{dt} = kV\).
Qadam 4: pani kam ho raha hai, is liye rate negative: \(\frac{dV}{dt} = -kV\), jahan \(k > 0\).
Dekha aap ne, wohi chaar qadam har jagah kaam karte hain.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Model wale sawalon mein examiner teen cheezein dekhta hai: sahi derivative (\(\frac{dP}{dt}\), \(\frac{dT}{dt}\), \(\frac{dq}{dt}\), ...), proportionality ko constant mein badalna, aur sahi sign. Hamesha pehle "\(\propto\)" wali line likhiye, phir "\(= k\)" wali line, aur saath likhiye ke \(k\) ke sign ka kya matlab hai. Is se aap ka jawab saaf aur poora lagta hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Growth/decay aur inflation/deflation: \(\frac{dP}{dt} = kP\) (\(k > 0\) izafa, \(k < 0\) kami, \(k = 0\) constant).
2. Newton's law of cooling/heating: \(\frac{dT}{dt} = k(T_{S} - T)\), \(k > 0\).
3. RC circuit (charging): \(RC\frac{dq}{dt} = CV_{S} - q\); is ke liye \(V_{C} = \frac{q}{C}\), \(V_{R} = IR\), \(I = \frac{dq}{dt}\).
4. RL circuit (charging): \(L\frac{dI}{dt} = V_{S} - RI\); is ke liye \(V_{L} = L\frac{dI}{dt}\), \(V_{R} = RI\).
5. Yeh sab first-order, first-degree differential equations hain.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Final jawab mein \(\propto\) ka nishan chhor dena; hamesha "\(= k\)" likhiye.
2. \(k > 0\) ke saath \(\frac{dT}{dt} = k(T - T_{S})\) likhna: is se garam cheez aur garam hoti jayegi, jo na-mumkin hai. \(k > 0\) ho to bracket \(T_{S} - T\) hona chahiye.
3. RC circuit mein \(I = \frac{dq}{dt}\) bhool jana; phir equation mein koi derivative hi nahi bachta.
4. Inductor ka voltage \(L\frac{dI}{dt}\) aur resistor ka voltage \(RI\) aapas mein mila dena.
